before.finding: First signal after OS spawn/resource creation but before assignment can orphan child/group or skip resource cleanup. Three acquisition methods fail old code; captured owned resources are rescued.

limitations: First catchable SIGTERM/SIGINT after handlers install, including normal cleanup. No SIGKILL, host failure, power loss or forced termination guarantee.
Docker command boundary simulated; actual Docker runtime unverified.
Local cleanup cases use actual Nginx/backend with a synthetic successful probe body to target cleanup precisely. Separate baseline/six controls use actual network probes.

Fetch cleanup cases use actual disposable children with synthetic successful envelopes; existing suite separately verifies actual HTTP slow-drip cancellation, child reaping and retained completed rows.
No GoDaddy, Discord, public TLS/DNS, SQL persistence/restore or native acceptance; no approval or independent-review claim.

Acquisition deferral delays cancellation through handle registration; bounded transient Docker CLI commands can defer up to their 30-second timeout, local git/Nginx checks up to five seconds, plus process scheduling/reaping overhead.
Spawn/other-resource injection fixtures target the post-create/pre-assignment interval deterministically; arbitrary interpreter/OS failure remains outside guarantees.
coverage: Real Nginx master and worker spawned before caller assignment; TERM/INT verifies master reaped, workers exited and truthful cleanup flags.
Real disposable source child spawned before caller assignment; TERM/INT verifies child reaped and both pipes closed.
Backend constructor, thread start, tempdir construction and stderr open each inject TERM/INT after creation before caller registration.
Transient bounded commands inject TERM/INT after actual Popen and verify reaping.
Previous normal-cleanup, active-body cancellation and repeated-signal cases remain passing.
